verdict.rationale: Deepgram documents the core pieces of a phone voice agent: system prompts, a choice of TTS voice model, a first-voice-agent quickstart, and a Twilio guide where a caller dials a number and talks to the agent. However, the phone number comes from Twilio, and you must run your own server to bridge Twilio audio to the Voice Agent WebSocket. Nothing evidences a sub-hour path to a first live call. Missing for 10: a native phone number without a third-party provider, a no-bridge-server telephony setup, and evidence of time-to-first-call within an hour.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a working phone voice agent — prompt, voice, and phone number — and take my first live call within an hour
